answer.rationale: Promotional pricing is explicitly ruled out by exp_73 results—40% targeted discount drove acquisition but destroyed 30-day retention via a cohort that did not survive renewal. This is precisely the failure mode we face with competitive price-matching today. Instead, we should deploy activation_messaging (memory_91 confirmed week-one engagement lift) combined with simplified onboarding (memory_31, exp_86 confirmed +3% retention) to focus on product-led value realization in at-risk SMB accounts. This addresses churn root cause (perceived value gap) rather than race-to-bottom pricing. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for retention but are slower-acting. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB churn crisis. A standard_experiment targeting churning SMB accounts with a cohesive onboarding simplification + in-product activation sequence preserves both near-term retention and long-term unit economics, while a price-match response would replicate the failed exp_73 pattern and worsen LTV across the full SMB segment.
